title: Designing with Functions
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to break a bigger program into small, well-named functions that each do one job.
learn: Split a program into focused functions
Combine helpers into one small program
idea: Good programs are built from small functions that each do one clear job. When something goes wrong, you can find the broken function quickly. When you want to reuse logic, you call the function again. Name functions for what they do: average, grade, print_report. Then wire them together.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change Ava's scores to 95, 95, 95. Press Run. Ava's line should show avg 95.0 grade A.

practice.text: Finish average and grade. Make print_report call both and print one line for Maya.
practice.hint: average should add the three scores and divide by 3. print_report already has avg and letter — put them in print().
practice.starterTip: Try return (a + b + c) / 3 in average, and print(name, "avg", avg, "grade", letter) in print_report.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if average returns the mean, grade returns a letter, print_report uses both, and a report line prints.

practice.text: Finish area(w, h) and describe(w, h). describe should call area and print the result. Call describe once.
practice.hint: area returns width times height. describe is ready — you need the return in area and one call to describe at the bottom.
practice.starterTip: Use return w * h in area, then add describe(4, 3) on a blank line at the end.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if area returns w*h, describe calls area and prints, and describe is called at least once.

quiz.question: Why write many small functions instead of one long block?

options.text: Small functions are easier to test, reuse, and fix
You need more functions to use return
Python requires at least three functions in every program

quiz.correct: Small, focused functions are easier to understand, reuse, and fix.
quiz.wrong: The real benefit is readability and reuse — each function does one clear job.

quiz.question: What makes a good function name?

options.text: A clear name that says what the function does

quiz.correct: Names like average or print_report tell readers the job.
quiz.wrong: Pick names that describe the function’s one job.

quiz.question: In a well-designed report program, where should the letter-grade rules live?

options.text: Inside one grade helper that others call

quiz.correct: Keep the grade rules in one function so every caller shares them.
quiz.wrong: One helper for grading keeps the design clean.

project.title: Student Report Card
project.desc: Build a tiny report card with separate functions: average of three scores, a letter grade from that average, and print_report that uses both. Use fixed numbers — no input().
